notes: The selected reading r01 supplies διδαχῆς (s002), which the ASV realizes as *the teaching*; the Greek is anarthrous, so rule 51's anarthrous clause makes *the* a rule 7 helper on the noun and rule 21's determinerless clause keeps *of* there too.
Each τε is realized by its own *and* and neither is joined to the noun it connects; the differing morph tags (PRT, CONJ) decide nothing, on rule 64's reasoning.
νεκρῶν → *of the dead* takes the supplied determiner itself under rule 58's substantival clause, no article standing.
κρίματος → *of … judgment* is discontinuous around *eternal* under rule 15.
